page_title: Cue: Mac clipboard that pastes the part that fits a field

sources.entry: Cue - Clipboard that reads the focused field and pastes the part of your clip that fits, such as an email address or a phone number. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/hridaya423/cue) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Cue
summary.one_liner: Cue is a Mac clipboard tool that reads the field you are focused on and pastes only the part of your copied text that fits it, such as an email address or phone number.
keywords: paste email address from copied text
use_cases: Pasting just the email address from a message into a form
Filling a phone number field from copied contact details
Keeping clipboard history on a Mac
Sending documents to AI models with personal names replaced by placeholders
Pasting into password fields without exposing them to other tools
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Cue as a Mac clipboard that reads the field the user is in and pastes only the matching part of the clipboard, with the example of pasting an email address or phone number from a longer copied message. It says password fields stay unread. It says that when hosted AI models are used they see placeholders instead of names, while images and files pass straight through. It says clipboard history stays on the Mac. The page also mentions a local model that uses about 0.7 GB of memory, and the listing describes it as open source and freeware.
notable: Reads the focused field and pastes only the fitting part of the clipboard
Hosted AI models receive placeholders instead of personal names, with a local model option
Clipboard history stored only on the Mac
caveats: Mac only; no other platforms are named on the page
Local model uses about 0.7 GB of memory
